slides.prompt: How much money? How many friends?
slides.hint: Why does money take much but friends take many?
slides.notes: 60-min Khamis lesson, Module p86. Deductive opening: pupils notice the contrast before any rule. Collect oral guesses, give nothing away.

slides.prompt: Can you count it, or not?
slides.feedback: Countable nouns take a plural. Uncountable nouns have one form.
slides.notes: Prerequisite check: countable/uncountable decides every quantifier today. Teacher clicks the category the class proposes. Grammar book: countable unit nouns vs mass nouns.

slides.answer: She has many friends. Many pupils joined the walk.
slides.feedback: Many plus plural countable nouns means a large number.
slides.notes: First pattern from pupil deduction. Elicit the rule before revealing. Grammar book Much-many: many with countable plurals.

slides.answer: There is not much time left. Do we have much sugar?
slides.feedback: Much plus uncountable nouns, mostly in negatives and questions.
slides.notes: Second pattern. Stress negatives/questions at elementary level per grammar book. Drill chorally.

slides.prompt: What about some, a few, a lot of?
slides.answer: I have some apples. I have a few books. There are a lot of cars.
slides.feedback: Some hides the number. A few is small and countable. A lot of is large.
slides.notes: Third pattern, Module p86 points 2-5. A lot of works for both kinds in affirmatives. Keep brisk; the 10 questions do the heavy lifting.

slides.sentence: We saw {{blank}} kittens near the drain.
slides.feedback: Kittens are countable, so many fits. Much needs an uncountable noun.
slides.notes: Volunteer 1. Click fills the blank inline; Reset clears it.

slides.feedback: Rice is uncountable, and questions take much.
slides.notes: Volunteer 2. Ask why many fails before revealing.

slides.feedback: Salt is uncountable, and negatives take much.

slides.sentence: There were {{blank}} pupils at the assembly.
slides.feedback: Pupils are countable and plural, so many fits.

slides.prompt: Question 5: He did not drink ___ juice.
slides.feedback: Juice is uncountable, and negatives take much.
slides.notes: Volunteer 5. Halfway checkpoint: ask the class to state the much/many rule so far.

slides.sentence: He picked {{blank}} mangoes: four for his family.
slides.feedback: Four is a small countable number, so a few fits.
slides.notes: Volunteer 6. Teach the number-clue strategy from Module section B.

slides.prompt: Question 7: They saw ___ durians: fifty at the stall.
slides.feedback: Fifty durians is a large countable number, so many fits.

slides.sentence: There is {{blank}} milk in the fridge.
slides.feedback: Milk is uncountable. Many milk is never correct.
slides.notes: Volunteer 8. Name the classic error many + uncountable explicitly.

slides.prompt: Question 9: She saved ___ coins: thirty in her box.
slides.feedback: Thirty coins is large and countable, so a lot of fits.
slides.notes: Volunteer 9. A little needs an uncountable noun, so it fails twice here.

slides.feedback: Water is uncountable and the number is unknown, so some fits.
slides.notes: Volunteer 10. Some for unknown exact number per Module p86 point 2.

slides.prompt: State the rule for much and many.
slides.notes: Exit evidence, oral, 3 min. Expected: many + plural countable; much + uncountable in negatives/questions. Gaps found here open Friday's refresh.
